title: Design System: Spring AI from Scratch

title.purpose: Section headings on home and in lessons.

label.purpose: Navigation, buttons, notes; always sentence case.

numeral.purpose: Module and lesson-part numbers, tabular figures.

code.purpose: Code files and sandbox code; no ligatures, never italic.

shadows.name: line-band
shadows.purpose: The inset bar of the 'this line' band, paired with a --code-highlight background.

motion.name: step-band
motion.purpose: Background, rail and node colour transitions on hero trace steps.

motion.name: trace-pass
motion.purpose: The single load pass of the request trace: out, round the tool loop, back; skipped under reduced motion.

narrative.overview: One call runs through the whole site. The home page opens with a request trace: one `ChatClient` call travelling from your service through the advisor chain (memory, the tool loop, RAG) to `ChatModel` and the provider, then back as a typed `Answer`, with each step labelled by the module that teaches it. A single pass runs the request out, round the tool loop once and back, and comes to rest on `ChatClient`, where the course starts. The green band that marks the selected step also marks the key lines in every code file and the changed lines in the provider switcher, so "this is the part that matters" looks the same everywhere on the site. Around the code, everything is quiet: white or slate-900 paper, slate prose in IBM Plex Sans, emerald used only for links, the primary action and position in a sequence. The density is that of good reference documentation: generous measure, clear section breaks, nothing decorative. Code surfaces are the only saturated color on the page and they carry it fully (Catppuccin token colors: Latte, darkened where needed, on a near-white box in light mode; Mocha on the slate-800 card color in dark mode), which keeps the emerald chrome from competing with syntax colors. The system rejects the generic course-site template: no gradient washes, no card grids for lists, no ALL-CAPS eyebrows, no monospace used as a costume for small labels, no `→` on links, no `A · B · C` meta strings.
keyCharacteristics: One visual language for "this line": a translucent green band with a 3px inset bar.
Catppuccin code surfaces that follow the site theme; slate and emerald for everything else.
JetBrains Mono only for real code; IBM Plex Sans for prose, labels and numerals.
Numbers only for real sequences (modules, the four lesson parts), set light and tabular.
Flat surfaces separated by hairline rules and tonal steps, not shadows.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Emerald is the only chrome color. Amber, rose, sky and violet appear only as Gotcha kinds (reliability, security, cost, migration), where the hue carries the meaning.

rules.name: The Code Owns Saturation Rule
rules.body: Syntax color lives inside code surfaces. Chrome around code stays slate so the two never compete.

rules.name: The Mono Is Code Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only where the text is code, a file name, or a value the reader would type. Small UI labels are Plex.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, label, button and badge is sentence case. No tracked uppercase.

rules.name: The Flat By Default Rule
rules.body: Don't add shadows to separate content. Use a rule, a tonal step or space.

dos: Do mark the important line with the green band and inset bar, wherever code appears.
Do keep emerald for links, the primary action, module numbers and the current position.
Do set numbers in Plex with tabular figures, and only for real sequences.
Do write every label in sentence case and every link as the thing it opens.
Do let tables and code scroll inside their column on phones.
Do show JSON indented, two spaces and one key per line, everywhere; keep Jackson's own output and log lines as they are.
Do let inline code break anywhere, with its background cloned on each line, so a long API name never widens the page.
donts: Don't use ALL-CAPS tracked eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't use monospace for small UI labels; mono is for code.
Don't append → to links or buttons, or join meta with middle dots.
Don't lay out lists as card grids or add gradient washes.
Don't use a near-black dark background; dark mode is slate-900.
Don't add fake window chrome (dots, title bars) to code or sandboxes.
Don't set code in italics or turn ligatures on.
